articles.title: A new mechanism for reading extra-long genes in neurons
articles.desc: Neurons in humans and other mammals express many exceptionally long genes, ranging from more than 100 kbp to more than 2 Mbp, that are important for forming synapses and neural circuits. In general, genetic information is read from DNA into RNA. This process is called transcription. The longer a gene is, the more time it takes to read from beginning to end. In addition, gene expression must be regulated at several steps. Neurons are therefore thought to require special mechanisms to read long genes accurately and stably, but the details of these mechanisms have remained unclear.
ents: genetic information is read from DNA into RNA

In laboratory food-choice tests, the tiny, stinging pests overwhelmingly chose cooked beef and sunflower seeds over water-packed tuna.

Neu ist heuer der Rechtsanspruch auf Ganztagsbetreuung für Grundschulkinder, der schrittweise eingeführt wird. Außerdem ändern sich die Regeln zur Smartphonenutzung. So dürfen Handys bis einschließlich zur siebten Klasse auf dem gesamten Schulgelände nicht mehr benutzt werden. Bisher galt das grundsätzliche Verbot digitaler Endgeräte an Grundschulen. articles.title: Researchers propose quantum Earth observation for photon-limited environments
articles.desc: Have you ever wondered what Earth observation satellites see when they look down at the deep ocean or a dense tropical forest during the dead of night? The answer, for the most part, is nothing. Standard optical sensors require a steady stream of light to function, and in these photon-limited regions, they hit a hard physical boundary. But what if we could rewrite the rules of optical imaging? By borrowing techniques from quantum photonics, we can push beyond these classical limits and unlock a fundamentally new way to observe the darkest and most hidden environments on our planet.

articles.title: Magma repeatedly breaks and heals during eruptions, microscopic evidence suggests

articles.title: ‘All of us are going to pay’: 30% of Americans are taking out BNPL loans to pay for groceries, and it’s probably going to cost you
articles.desc: In the check-out line of your local grocery store, there’s a nearly one-in-three chance someone there has used an app like Klarna or Affirm to finance their purchase of produce, milk, and eggs at some point. Their use of buy now, pay later could mean your groceries are about to cost more, economists have found. A study from the Washington University in St. Louis, which will be published in the next issue of the Management Science journal, found that as more consumers turn to buy now, pay later to purchase their necessities, retailers may actually increase prices and slash inventory as a result

articles.title: Can Independent Testing Make AI Safer?
articles.desc: Vals AI co-founder and CEO Rayan Krishnan says investment in testing and evaluating AI hasn’t kept pace with the rapid improvement in model capabilities. His firm independently evaluates models from companies including OpenAI and Anthropic, and sees early signs of AI moving toward recursive self-improvement, though models remain well behind top human researchers today. articles.title: Trump says Ukraine and Russia agreed to halt strikes on energy. Zelenskyy is not so sure.
articles.desc: KYIV — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has poured cold water on his American counterpart Donald Trumps claim that Ukraine and Russia have agreed to halt strikes on each others energy infrastructure. Trump over the weekend blamed Kyiv’s strikes on Moscow’s refineries — not the U.S.-Israel war on Iran — for high diesel prices, then on Monday said Ukraine and Russia had agreed to halt attacks on energy targets. Ukraine, though, is skeptical. Russia has been barraging Ukraine’s ports, energy grid, fuel stations, and logistics with dozens of jet-powered drones and missiles for several years
